question: What will be New England's spark spread on December 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: EIA/ISO-NE early-December New England on-peak spark spreads (E-7G). Monthly-average spreads were ~46 (Dec 2025, gas ~$14.9), ~34 (Dec 2024, gas ~$9), ~17 (Dec 2023, mild). Current spot on Nov 5, 2026 is 46.99/1.35 → 37.5; Henry Hub Dec <$3, Algonquin winter strip ~$11.67 with the premium peaking in January, and a mild NOAA outlook. The spread is fairly gas-level-invariant because power tracks gas at heat rates around 8.5-10. Median ~31, with tails for cold-snap gas spikes (low/negative) and power spikes (>65). No human market found; the harness candidate (a Polymarket New England Revolution soccer match) is unrelated.

Algonquin spot recently ~$1.3-2.1 on mild weather and an operational flow order from Nov 1.
- PremierEnergy Nov 2, 2026: NYMEX Dec below $3.00 on mild forecasts and a big storage build.
- NOAA winter 2026/27 outlook favors warmer than normal in New England.
- Kilowattlogic: Apr-Jul 2026 Algonquin traded $0.43 under Henry Hub; record Canadian imports; more renewables.
- Mechanisms: cold snap → gas spikes can outpace power (narrow or negative spread); power-side scarcity → spread above 65. Carbon (RGGI) adds ~$7/MWh floor-ish to the spread.
- Not found: EIA daily historical Dec 1 values (xlsx download not executed); current Mass Hub Dec forward; any prediction market on this.

calls.reasoning: As of the Nov 5, 2026 EIA Daily Prices, Algonquin was $1.35 and Mass Hub $46.99 (spread $37.54), with gas depressed by a regional glut and mild weather. December normally brings the winter gas premium: the winter strip was ~$11.67 on Oct 29, with forwards peaking near $16 in Dec-Jan. Higher gas usually compresses E-7G because power's implied heat rate does not scale linearly with gas. A warm NOAA outlook and surplus supply argue for moderate Dec 1 spot gas (~$3-10), which historically gives spreads of ~$20-45. The low tail (cold snap, gas >$15) can push the spread below $10 or negative; the high tail is a power spike while gas stays cheap. No human market found (only an unrelated Polymarket soccer contract).

calls.reconciliation: All three runs shared the same facts (11/5/26 EIA values, winter strip ~$11.67, warm outlook, glut) and medians of 30-31. Disputes were judgment calls on how much mass to put past the bounds and on width. The one open factual point, the December Algonquin forward ($8.686 snippet vs peaks near $16), could not be settled without web access, so I kept that uncertainty in the distribution. I took median 31, a 10-90 band close to the runs' consensus, the low-tail escape at 9% (a cold snap compressing the spread is a real mechanism, but the warm outlook and glut temper it) and the high-tail escape at 6%.
